Alibabaが開発した「Wan-Streamer」が本当に凄いです！✨

これは映像、音声、テキストをひとつのモデルでまとめて処理できる「オムニモーダル（複数の異なる種類の情報を同時に扱えること）」なAIシステムなんです。

驚くべきは、人間と会話しているのと変わらない「約550ms（v0.2ではなんとモデル遅延約200ms！）」という超低遅延でのスムーズな双方向のやり取りを実現している点です。

この爆速処理の秘密は「Thinker-Performer」という独自構造にあります。💡
頭脳となって素早く論理を組み立てる役割（Thinker）と、映像を作り出す重い処理を担う役割（Performer）を分離することで、圧倒的なスピードと動画品質を両立させているのですね！

さらに、決まったアバターに縛られず、テキストの指示（プロンプト）次第で人間、動物、アニメキャラなど、どんな姿でも一瞬で具現化して話せます。

オンライン接客やバーチャル対話が、SFの世界から一気に現実になりそうでワクワクしちゃいます！🚀

content:
【ローカル完結型MV制作！自動で音と同期する「ltxmv」パイプラインが凄すぎる！】
ローカルのRTX 4090環境で、音楽解析から高品質なミュージックビデオ（MV）生成までを自動で行う驚きのパイプライン「ltxmv」が登場しました！🎬✨

このシステムの何が凄いかというと、音楽のビートや構成（イントロ、サビなど）を自作の解析ツールで自動で読み解き、それに合わせて映像のカット割りを自動制御してくれるんです！音楽と映像がバッチリ同期したMVが作れちゃいますね。🎵

注目の映像生成スタックは、
1. Ideogram 4.0で高画質なベース静止画を生成 🖼️
2. LTX-Video 2.3で静止画を滑らかな動画へ変換（i2v） 🎥
3. SeedVR2でシネマティックに高精細化（アップスケール） 🌟
という、まさに最強の最適ルート！

さらに、キャラクターの顔を固定する「Nano Banana 2」や選択的なリップシンク、そして細かな動きだけをサクッと修正できるモジュール式のプロンプト管理など、商業レベルのクオリティを担保する工夫が満載です。

音楽に合わせた映像制作の工数を劇的に減らして、個人のローカル環境でここまで完結させられるなんて、これからのAI映像制作の未来が本当に楽しみになりますね！🚀

驚くべき技術が登場しました！なんと、284Bという超弩級の規模を持つ「DeepSeek-V4 Flash」を、RTX 6000 AdaやRTX 5090といった単一のGPU環境で爆速で動かせる最適化実装「vLLM-Moet」が公開されています！🚀

本来ならH100などの超高額なエンタープライズGPUサーバーが複数枚必要になるモンスターモデルなのですが、この実装を使えば個人のワークステーションでも120 t/sを超える驚異的なスピードで動作可能になります。自宅や社内の機密データを外に出さずに、最高峰の推論能力をローカルで独占できるのは夢のようですね！✨

この魔法のような高速化を支える技術が本当に素晴らしいんです！
1️⃣ 「Routed Experts」の2-bit圧縮 ＆ FP4のハイブリッド量子化
MoE（混合専門家）構造の特性を活かし、トークンが動的に割り振られる部分を極限の2-bitまで圧縮しつつ、精度維持に必要な箇所はFP4で保持することで、画期的なVRAM節約と精度維持を両立しています。
2️⃣ 投機的サンプリング（MTP）の導入
一度の処理で複数のトークンを予測する技術により、文字の生成速度を劇的に向上させています。

長い会話（最大128K〜256Kコンテキスト）でもメモリ消費を抑え込み、実用性を高めています。

注意点として、モデルを読み込む際に一時的に約150GBという大容量のシステムメモリ（RAM）が必要になるため、十分なメモリの用意やスワップ設定が必要になりますが、一度GPUメモリ（VRAM）に入ってしまえば、あとは完全にGPU内で快適に動作します！

【LLMの量子化レベルを徹底比較！Döner Benchで見るモデル性能とトレードオフの実態】

「Döner Style kebab skewer（ドネルケバブの串）」を回転させるHTMLをライブラリなしで作成するという、ユニークで面白いベンチマーク「Döner Bench」の第2回が公開されました！💡

今回は、Qwen 3.6やGemma 4といった人気ローカルLLMを対象に、異なる量子化（Quantization）レベルでどのような性能差が出るのかが検証されています。
量子化というのは、モデルのデータ容量を軽量化してPCでの動作をスムーズにする素晴らしい技術ですが、これによって性能がどう変化するかが一目でわかる興味深い内容となっています！✨

評価の結果、やはり「Gemma 4」をはじめとする各モデルで、量子化レベルが極端に低くなると（特にIQ2レベルなど）、出力のばらつきが大きくなったりエラーが起きやすくなったりと、性能低下が目立つ結果になりました。
一方で、「Qwen 3.6 35B A3B Q8 K XL」は比較的安定した結果を見せてくれたようですね！💪

軽量化と性能のトレードオフは、ローカルLLMを導入する上で避けて通れないテーマ。
タスクのランダム性もあるため解釈には少し注意が必要ですが、モデル選びの非常に参考になる比較データですね！😊

【動画編集が劇的に爆速化！ComfyUI-Sequencerでロスレスカット＆トランジションを実現！】
ComfyUIで生成した動画の繋ぎ合わせや編集に悩んでいませんか？✨

このツールの凄いところは、強力な動画処理エンジンである「FFmpeg」をベースにしているため、圧倒的な処理速度を誇る点です🎥

なんと、5分間の動画2本（計10分）を繋ぐ処理が「約0.8秒」で完了する驚異のスピードです！

2️⃣ **トランジション効果**
カットの繋ぎ目に、ディゾルブやワイプ、フェードなどの切り替え効果を簡単に追加できます。
10分の動画にエフェクトを適用しても約82秒で完了するので、実時間より7倍以上も高速に処理できちゃいます！

content:
法人向けの生成AI研修をやっている受講生さんから、経理の自動化で月「15〜16時間」浮いたという報告が来ました。

正直、地味に見えるかもしれません。でも、これマジで強いです。

何をしたか。Claude Codeで、領収書と請求書の処理を丸ごと自動化する仕組みを作りました。

【Before】月150件を、全部手作業で仕訳
・担当の税理士さんはややご年配で、freeなどのクラウドは使っていない
・紙の領収書は丸投げ、オンライン分はjpgとPDFで送られてくる
・月150件くらいの証憑がGoogleドライブと現物とPCにバラバラ
・それを全部、人の手で仕訳していた

　1件あたり5〜10分。月150件で、だいたい「17.5時間」。毎月それだけの時間が、ただの入力作業で消えていました。

【After】同じ150件を、確認するだけ
・毎晡21:03に自動で動いて、PDFや画像を読み取る
・ファイル名を命名規則どおりにリネーム
・キーワード辞書12カテゴリとAIの二段構えで勘定科目まで自動で判定
・決算用のExcelに追記して、処理済みフォルダに移すところまで一気通貫

　担当者がやることは、領収書をスマホで撮ってフォルダに入れるだけ。税理士さんは、上がってきたExcelとデータを厳密にチェックするだけ。

　月17.5時間の作業が、確認だけの月1〜2時間に。差し引き、月15〜16時間の削減です。

───────────

で、ここがAIをあまり触っていない人に伝わりづらいところ。

これ、ただ「作業が速くなった」って話じゃないです。

分類ミスや転記漏れのリスクがほぼゼロになって、誰がやっても同じ結果が出る。人が必ず出すミスと、その人にしかできないという属人性を、まとめて仕組みで潰しています。

浮いた15〜16時間は、また別の改善に回せる。時間が減っただけじゃなくて、次に進むための時間が生まれた。ここまで来ると、AI活用はかなり強いです。

しかもこの受講生さん、自称「バリバリの文系」。開発できない、コード読めない、黒い画面にいまだにびびってる、という状態からのスタートでした。それでも講座の動画をじっくり見て、その場で手を動かして、詰まったら都度質問して、ここまで作り切った。

講座のLIVEセミナーでもよく話すんですが、AIは、時間の余裕がない人ほど効きます。定常業務をAIに任せて、空いた時間をゼロイチの仕事に回す。この受講生さんは、それを経理という一番地味な現場でやり切った人です。

こういう報告が現場から上がってくるのが、この仕事の一番楽しいところです。

The hottest take in AI right now: the IDE is becoming the operating system for autonomous agents.

Claude Code's new desktop launch isn't another coding assistant.

It's an attempt to replace the entire developer workflow.

One app now has:

• Parallel AI coding sessions with Git isolation
• Browser, terminal, editor and diff in one workspace
• Autonomous testing and self-verification
• Background cloud sessions that keep working after you close your laptop
• CI monitoring and auto-merge
• Phone-to-code dispatching
• Connectors, MCP servers and plugins

The important shift isn't "Claude can code."

It's that Claude is starting to:

understand → build → test → debug → review → ship

with increasingly little human intervention.

We're moving from:

copilot → coworker → autonomous software engineer.

I don't think the winners of this decade will be the models with the best autocomplete.

They'll be the systems that can own the entire software development loop.

content:
I've previously tried to rebut this argument as a kind of rebranding of arrogance as humility, especially around COVID (see https://t.co/bQ9XFSel5k ). As COVID was ramping up, people kept saying it would be insufficiently "humble" to take any action against it, because we hadn't yet "proven" that it could become a worldwide pandemic. As there became a 10% chance, a 25% chance, and then a 50% chance that it would, people continued not to take action, because there still wasn't the "proof", and it would be "arrogant" to prepare for something that merely had a 25% chance of killing millions of people.

But this is the wrong way of thinking about things. The people who were implicitly acting as if there was a 100% chance that COVID wouldn't be dangerous, were calling the people assuming a 75% chance that it wouldn't be "arrogant" and accusing them of being "absolutely sure" that it would be dangerous! 

If you allowed a 10% or 25% or even a 1% chance that AI could be dangerous, I think you would be extremely invested in building the global capacity for a potential off switch - not necessarily in pulling that off switch now, but in making sure it existed and can be pulled on short notice. That's AI2040's current ask - building the technology to verify an agreement if it needs to happen later. It's the only thing that needs to be done before the situation clarifies in 2027 or 2028. I think if you are indeed trying to being humble and leave room for all possibilities, you should refocus on supporting it.

Also, we at least have lines on graphs suggesting our position might be right. Where's your argument that regulating chips the same way we regulate every other product would lead to a "global surveillance state"? When it's about blocking AI safety, all people require is hand-waving; when it's about trying to create the capacity for it, no argument, no matter how strong, will ever be good enough.

title: The Future of Genus Patenting Strategies for Antibodies Post-Amgen
content: Broad functional genus claiming was previously a standard strategy for innovators seeking IP protection for antibodies. Prior guidance from the USPTO, including the “newly characterized antigen” test, encouraged broad claiming of antibodies based upon their function alone. For decades, that effectively allowed innovators to claim much more than they in fact discovered in practice. In the wake of the Supreme Court’s Amgen decision, courts have adopted the reasoning articulated in Amgen to strike down functional genus antibody claims for lacking either enablement or written description. title: UN rights office urges Sri Lanka to investigate deadly prison violence amid torture allegations
content: The UN Human Rights Office on Friday urged Sri Lankan authorities to conduct a prompt, independent and transparent investigation into recent incidents of prison violence following deadly clashes and allegations of torture involving transferred inmates. UN Human Rights Office spokesperson Ravina Shamdasani called for accountability after violence erupted at Negombo Prison on July 5, leaving at least 28 people dead, including seven prison officials, and injuring more than 100 others. According to authorities, the prison was built to house approximately 640 inmates but reportedly held around 2,400 at the time of the unrest, highlighting longstanding concerns over severe overcrowding. Earlier this week, the Sri Lankan government announced that it had established a three-member committee to investigate the violence. However, concerns continued to escalate after local media reported the deaths of two inmates who had been transferred from Negombo following the clashes. One inmate died at Boossa High Security Prison on July 8 after reportedly suffering a “sudden illness,” while another inmate transferred to Agunukolapelessa Prison also died the same day. The Committee to Protect Rights of Prisoners alleged that inmates transferred from Negombo had been subjected to torture and other forms of ill-treatment while in custody. In response, the Human Rights Commission of Sri Lanka (HRCSL) issued a statement directing the Commissioner General of Prisons to ensure the safety of detainees and grant the commission unrestricted access to prison facilities to investigate the allegations. Amnesty International also expressed concern over the reported deaths and allegations of abuse. title: DOJ sues Maryland for obstructing federal immigration enforcement
content: The US Department of Justice (DOJ) filed a lawsuit against the state of Maryland and Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown on Thursday, alleging that the state’s Community Trust Act obstructs federal immigration enforcement in violation of the Supremacy Clause of the US Constitution. The complaint, filed in the US District Court for the District of Maryland, asks the court to declare the law invalid and to permanently enjoin its enforcement. The DOJ brings four counts, all grounded in the Supremacy Clause. Two allege preemption. First, the department contends the Act is expressly preempted by 8 USC § 1373 and 8 USC § 1644 , which bar states from restricting the exchange of immigration status information with federal officials. Second, the DOJ argues separately that the Act is preempted as an obstacle to the federal enforcement scheme. The remaining counts invoke the intergovernmental immunity doctrine , alleging the Act (1) unlawfully regulates the federal government by demanding judicial warrants that federal law does not require for civil immigration arrests and (2) discriminates against it by singling out federal immigration authorities. The complaint leans on Arizona v. United States , where the US Supreme Court in 2012 affirmed the federal government’s preeminent authority over immigration. The DOJ says that the law has already produced operational consequences, pointing to instances in which facilities declined to transfer individuals to federal custody in response to detainers. Enacted this year as emergency legislation, the Community Trust Act , restricts when state and local officers may cooperate with federal immigration authorities. Correctional facilities may not notify federal authorities that an individual is in custody, hold a person past their release, or transfer them to immigration officials absent a valid court order or judicial warrant. title: UN rights expert urges rejection of France bill presuming legality of lethal force by police officers
content: A UN expert on Wednesday called on the French government to throw out a bill that would enshrine the presumption that police officers who use firearms are acting within the scope of their duties unless evidence proves otherwise, a decision that could legitimize and normalize violence against civilians. In commenting on the potential consequences if this bill passes and becomes law, Morris Tidball-Binz, UN Special Rapporteur on extrajudicial, summary or arbitrary executions stated: The duty to investigate every potentially unlawful killing rests with the State… It cannot be displaced, in law or in practice, by requiring victims or their families to rebut a legal presumption that the use of potentially lethal force was lawful before the facts have been independently established. Draft bill 691, which establishes the presumption of lawful shooting for authorities using their weapons was passed in its first reading by the French National Assembly, and it now heads to the Senate, which is the upper house of the French Parliament. In one of its earlier drafts, the wording of the bill was drafted as a “presumption of self-defense” under the Penal Code, but later it was rewritten to modify the Code of Security. Having been approved by 313 votes to 199 at the most recent reading of the bill, its supporters largely say that by giving enforcement officers the benefit of the doubt in shooting cases, it protects them from unnecessary criminal liability. However, critics have stated that the new legal presumption would shift the burden of proof and require victims’ families and prosecutors to prove that a shooting was neither proportionate nor necessary. This, in turn, could grant officers institutional impunity , and could lead to an increase in fatal shootings and a decline in public trust. title: Google's New Remote Attestation Scheme is As Bad As Its Old One
content: Google owes its existence to the open web, but today, its technological “innovations” have much to do with locking users into a “walled garden.” The latest of these is “ reCAPTCHA Mobile Verification ,” an experimental initiative that will let companies block users if they are running independent, "de-googled" versions of Android. These “indie Android” versions are favored by people who want to protect their privacy and their attention by blocking trackers and ads. Worse, this is just the latest in a line of similarly user-hostile measures. Long before “agentic AI,” we had the idea that software would act as your agent on the internet. That's why the old-fashioned technical term for a browser is a “user agent.” Your browser acts on your behalf to retrieve information and then show it to you, in the format you choose. It's your agent . This is a powerful and profound idea. It is because browsers are our “agents” that we expect them to accept our directives, say, by blocking pop-ups, or by turning off autoplay sound, or by blocking commercial surveillance trackers . Your browser does all that because your browser works for you . The reason your browser can work for you is that the web is an open, standardized technology. In theory, anyone who follows the standards published by the World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) can make a browser, and that web browser can connect to any web server. Browsers and servers are interoperable . It's the same force that means you can put anyone's gas in your gas-tank, or anyone's shoelaces in your shoes, or anyone's milk on your cereal. But what if manufacturers could dictate those choices to you? What if your light socket refused to use a lightbulb unless it was officially blessed by the socket's manufacturer? What if your dishwasher refused to wash your dishes unless you bought them from one of the manufacturer's “dish partners?” What if your toaster refused to toast “unauthorized bread?” It's hard to see how a company could win its marke
